issues.title: Direct malloc instead of zmalloc
issues.description: The rule requires using zmalloc() wrapper for memory allocation, but malloc() was used directly in the cluster initialization code
issues.rule_name: Use zmalloc/zfree Wrappers Instead of Direct malloc/free

issues.title: Incorrect operation order causes potential data loss during cluster verification
issues.description: The verifyClusterConfigWithData() function executes clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots() before clusterClaimUnassignedSlots(). This reverses the intended logic: the function should first claim ownership of unassigned slots that contain keys (preventing orphaned data), then delete keys from slots that are genuinely owned by other nodes. With this bug, keys in unassigned slots may be incorrectly deleted before the node has a chance to claim ownership, resulting in permanent data loss during cluster startup or recovery scenarios.

issues.title: ASM cron runs before cluster state update causing stale state issues
issues.description: The serverCron() function now calls asmCron() before clusterCron(). This is problematic because clusterCron() contains the call to clusterUpdateState() which updates the cluster's operational state (CLUSTER_OK vs CLUSTER_FAIL). ASM (Atomic Slot Migration) operations depend on having an accurate view of the cluster state to make correct migration decisions. By executing asmCron() first, migration tasks may operate on stale cluster state information from the previous iteration, potentially leading to incorrect slot migration decisions, failed migrations, or data consistency issues during cluster rebalancing operations.

issues.title: Internal helper function clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots missing static declaration
issues.description: The function clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots() is defined and used only within cluster.c (no external callers, not declared in any header file), but lacks the 'static' keyword. According to AGENTS.md Rule #7, all internal helper functions that are not part of the public API must be declared static to enforce proper encapsulation and prevent symbol pollution. This violation could lead to naming conflicts in large codebases and breaks the repository's explicit encapsulation requirements.

issues.title: Non-static internal helper function exported from cluster.c
issues.description: `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots()` is introduced as a file-local helper and is only used within `src/cluster.c` (called by `verifyClusterConfigWithData()`), but it is declared without `static`, unnecessarily exporting the symbol outside this compilation unit. Per the rule, internal helper functions must be declared `static`.
issues.rule_name: Rule 7: Internal Helper Functions Must Be Declared Static

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14587 - Refactor some of ASM and slot-stats functions

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves shared cluster logic out of `cluster_legacy.c`. It adds `clusterCommonInit()` for slot-stats and ASM setup, moves the `asmCron`/`asmBeforeSleep` calls into `server.c`, and moves CLUSTER MIGRATION/SYNCSLOTS dispatch into the generic `clusterCommand`. It also splits `verifyClusterConfigWithData()` into a shared part in `cluster.c` and two helpers: `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots` (shared) and `clusterClaimUnassignedSlots` (legacy). The description says nothing about behavior changes.

That claim doesn't hold. The split helpers run in the wrong order. Delete runs first, and its skip check (`clusterIsMySlot || importing`) doesn't exempt slots with no owner, so keys in unassigned slots get deleted at startup. The original code would have claimed those slots instead. That's silent data loss. Smaller drift: the slot-stats array is now allocated with raw `malloc` instead of `zmalloc`, and `asmCron` now runs before `clusterCron` instead of after.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new order in verifyClusterConfigWithData deletes keys that the old code kept by claiming their slots. That's data loss in a PR that says it changes no behavior. The malloc/zmalloc swap is also an unintended change.

architecture.overview:
Redis Cluster has a shared layer (`cluster.c`, which holds the generic CLUSTER command and helpers like `clusterIsMySlot` and `getImportingSlotSource`) and a mechanism-specific layer (`cluster_legacy.c`, which holds the gossip bus, `server.cluster` state, `clusterInit`, `clusterCron`, and `clusterBeforeSleep`). Atomic slot migration (ASM, `cluster_asm.c`) and slot stats used to be wired up from inside the legacy layer.

This PR moves that wiring up a level. `main()` now calls a new `clusterCommonInit()`, which allocates slot stats, resets them, and calls `asmInit`, before calling `clusterInit()`. `serverCron` and `beforeSleep` now call `asmCron` and `asmBeforeSleep` directly. MIGRATION and SYNCSLOTS are dispatched in the generic `clusterCommand`. The startup check `verifyClusterConfigWithData()` now lives in `cluster.c`: it validates DB0 and then calls two helpers. `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots` is shared and deletes keys in slots owned by other nodes. `clusterClaimUnassignedSlots` is legacy-specific and adds slots that have no owner to `myself`, then saves the config.
steps: `server.c` `main()`: when cluster is enabled, it now calls `clusterCommonInit()` (slot-stats allocation, `resetClusterStats`, `asmInit`) before `clusterInit()`.
`cluster_legacy.c` `clusterInit()`: it no longer resets stats or initializes ASM; it only builds `server.cluster` and loads nodes.conf.
`server.c` `serverCron` / `beforeSleep`: they now call `asmCron()` and `asmBeforeSleep()` next to `clusterCron()` and `clusterBeforeSleep()`, instead of having the legacy functions call them.
`cluster.c` `clusterCommand`: it handles `migration` and `syncslots` before falling through to `clusterCommandSpecial`.

After `loadDataFromDisk()`, `verifyClusterConfigWithData()` in `cluster.c` checks DB0 only, then calls `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots()` followed by `clusterClaimUnassignedSlots()` from `cluster_legacy.c`. The order of these two calls matters.

findings.title: Keys in unassigned slots are deleted before they can be claimed (data loss at startup)
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/cluster.c`, `verifyClusterConfigWithData()` (around lines 2209-2213) calls `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots()` before `clusterClaimUnassignedSlots()`. The delete helper doesn't skip slots with no owner (`clusterIsMySlot` is false when `getNodeBySlot(i)` is NULL), so keys in unassigned slots are deleted before they can be claimed. This is a regression from the original single loop in `cluster_legacy.c`. Swap the two calls so `clusterClaimUnassignedSlots()` runs first. Also harden `clusterDeleteKeysInUnownedSlots()` (around line 2151) to skip slots where `getNodeBySlot(i) == NULL`, so the order no longer matters. Add a cluster test that restarts a primary with keys in a slot that has no owner and asserts the keys survive and the slot is assigned to that node.

findings.title: Slot-stats array now allocated with raw malloc instead of zmalloc
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/cluster.c`, `clusterCommonInit()` (around line 2138) allocates `server.cluster_slot_stats` with raw `malloc`. Before this PR, `src/server.c` `main()` used `zmalloc`. Change it back to `zmalloc` so the allocation is counted in Redis memory accounting and uses the standard OOM handling. That matches the rest of the cluster code.

findings.title: asmCron now runs before clusterCron instead of after
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/server.c` `serverCron()` (around lines 1656-1660), the refactor calls `asmCron()` before `clusterCron()`. Before this PR it ran at the end of `clusterCron()`. Swap them so `clusterCron()` runs first and then `asmCron()`. That keeps the original ordering and matches the `beforeSleep` hook order.

findings.title: Good separation of shared vs mechanism-specific cluster logic
findings.body: Moving ASM init, cron, and before-sleep hooks, plus MIGRATION/SYNCSLOTS dispatch, out of `cluster_legacy.c` into `server.c` and `cluster.c` makes sense. Another cluster implementation now gets ASM and slot stats without copying that wiring. Running `asmInit()` before `clusterInit()` is also safer, because nodes.conf loading now runs with `asmManager` already initialized. Both helpers use accessor functions (`getMyClusterNode`, `getImportingSlotSource`, `clusterIsMySlot`) instead of touching `server.cluster` directly, which keeps them usable by other implementations.
